vi.reason: The relative clause 'do AI' is grammatically unfinished. Name AI's writing explicitly, and attach the compile-time clause to the Rocq kernel's examination of that proof. The selected wording retains kernel, Rocq, AI authorship and compile time.

Make the memory restriction explicitly a requirement on the admitted input, rather than a bare assertion that input never exceeds memory. Retain the system model, ordinary build and specified memory allowance. 'phai' restores the premise's must-condition.
An input does not itself exit or return a value. State that for every input the program exits and returns limit plus 1, while retaining the result in the return column.

'Hai so 8 la cung mot viec' is an unnatural literal rendering of treating two eights as the same thing. Use the ordinary Vietnamese verb for conflating them; keep the conversion-at-storage location and the two eights.
'Du tien de' is an unnatural way to say that this premise is satisfied. Use 'thoa tien de'; retain the conditional, both builds, negation and only the designated errors.

'Hai dong' can be understood as two record rows, but is also easy to confuse with two code lines just discussed. Naming the two results directly is clearer; this is not a claimed factual contradiction.

The original meaning is recoverable. 'Bieu dien' makes the mathematical encoding of the same input in eight true/false bits more natural than 'viet cung dau vao thanh'. No model strength or checker is added.

th.reason: At the end of the current relative clause, 'while compiling' can modify AI writing the proof. Put compile time first so the kernel performs the check during compilation. Keep the full kernel term, Rocq, proof and AI-written authorship. The clear candidate remains over 36 and is unresolved.
Replace only the storage preposition with 'in'. Preserve complete calculation value, stored total, integer, unsignedness and 16 bits.

Fill the return value in the already named return field, using another independent counting program. State explicitly that its input is the limit. 'Counting' is already carried by the program, so the limit remains its counting limit; no downstream relation to the guard is introduced.
Move 'same program' before the ordinary/error-checking forms and avoid repeating 'version'. Retain public release, the same program, both forms and the explicit not-before/after-repair distinction.

The current meaning is correct. The shorter candidate still preserves system model, input must-condition, ordinary build, non-exceedance and specified memory budget. It remains over 54; no faithful natural in-budget version is offered.
Use an explicit if-condition and 'both' referring to the two builds. Keep the absence of the designated errors, rather than promising absence of every possible error.

Keep finite length of the behavioral record, possibility, text, the program as emitter and already-produced output. The clear shorter noun phrase remains over 52. A finite number of records or short records would change the claim and is not proposed.

'This conclusion' explicitly refers to the immediately preceding termination-proof statement. Restrict that conclusion to this public release and exclude the entire research from its scope. This preserves the source's anaphoric limitation without repeating the termination noun and does not assert that the wider research proved termination.
Use the Thai term for a line of code, not a table row: this question points to the line that preserves the total. Keep the found counterexample and complete total.
This is the entire code line, not a record-table row. Retain both calculation and the conversion used to store the total as changes to that line.
Make the program the subject that exits and returns the bound plus 1 for every input, rather than saying that the inputs exit. Retain the completed return-column result and the universal input scope.
